title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows and optimize cache parallelism
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: Our monolithic CI workflows (lint+test+release) have grown slow and brittle as repositories and matrix sizes expanded. This PR splits the workflows into three focused pipelines (lint, test, release), reduces wasted work by gating release workflows, and improves cache parallelism to speed up matrix runs. Changes include: 1) split .github/workflows/ci.yml into ci-lint.yml, ci-test.yml, release.yml; 2) extract shared job templates to .github/workflows/templates/ to reduce duplication; 3) enable restored cache keys with parallel cache uploads for build/test matrices; 4) add a lightweight fast-failure lint job earlier in the pipeline to provide quick feedback; 5) update README/CONTRIBUTING notes for local workflow run commands. Compatibility and rollout: This is backwards-compatible for developers (same exit codes and artifacts). We are enabling the new workflows behind a short feature window and will monitor flakiness for two weeks before deprecating the old monolithic workflow. Testing: validated on redwood (monorepo) and sdk repositories with small matrix sizes; observed ~25-40% median improvement in total pipeline time for PRs that previously ran full matrix. Checklist: - [x] Split workflows and moved templates - [x] Added fast-fail lint job - [x] Implemented parallel cache upload and improved keying - [x] Updated docs and local run instructions - [x] Ran canary on internal repos and observed stable results - [x] Tests and linters green in CI Notes: Cache parallelism increases concurrent artifact upload but keeps TTL and restore semantics intact (uses primary+secondary key strategy). Release workflow now requires the test workflow to pass and waits on a manual approval step for production releases. Related: ENG-4821 (ci scale), ENG-4870 (release automation hygiene).

review_comments: Ravi Patel: Can we keep the old monolithic workflow for one week as a fallback during rollout?
Ava Martinez: Yes — I added a short-lived flag and kept the old workflow file for 7 days. We'll delete after monitoring.
Sofia Chen: The cache key needs the node version and matrix hash to avoid cross-job collisions. Please include node-version in the primary key.
Ava Martinez: Updated cache helper to include node-version and matrix hash. Also added a secondary key fallback for partial restores.
Liam O'Connor: Observed a flaky integration test on the canary runs. Recommend adding a 30s retry wrapper rather than skipping the test.
Ava Martinez: Added retry with exponential backoff for the failing step and documented the rationale in the commit message.
release_notes: Refactor CI workflows: split lint/test/release pipelines, improved cache parallelism and keying, added fast-fail lint job; reduces PR pipeline time and improves maintainability.
notes_for_ops: Monitor main CI queue latency and cache hit rates for two weeks. If cache hit rate drops >10% after rollout, revert parallel upload or refine keying. Ensure old workflow removal is coordinated with infra on 2026-02-22.
performance_observation: Canary runs showed a 30% median reduction in total runtime for typical PRs and a 15% improvement on heavy matrix builds due to parallelized cache uploads and smaller job startup times.
